smell_validity.evidence: The same conceptual param groups (request-assembly 5 params, response-assembly 4 params, query, headers) recur as separate parameters through each flavor's helper signatures across 3 request and 3 response flavors. The values belong together (one stage's inputs) yet are threaded as unrelated pieces. diff_desc draws the boundary: extract-method is reasonable; the parameter threading is the smell.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Adding an event flavor copies each stage's parameter list again; changing an assembly input forces updating duplicate signatures in agreement. The clumps repeatedly obscure that each stage's inputs are one concept across all flavors. A shared stage-data abstraction would restore a clear ownership boundary and make future flavor additions safer, beyond a mere local edit.

development_plausibility.evidence: The change models a natural extract-method pass: inline conversion stages pulled into named, documented per-flavor helpers taking their values as explicit params — exactly what extract-method produces. Real flavor differences (ALB's commented-out GO_API_HOST, V2 cookie/comma-split headers) justify the per-accessor shape. Style, terminology, and placement fit the existing core package.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt names the recurring clumps and scope, requires replacing every instance, and preserves implementation freedom (struct, record, or shared helper). Its preservation boundary is exceptionally specific — GO_API_HOST honor rules per flavor, error-message capitalization, V2 cookie/comma-split handling — decisively preventing costly wrong direction, incomplete cleanup, and irrelevant redesign.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Four distinct clump purposes exist: request-assembly, response-assembly, query, and header propagation. At least two need different decisions: query (multi-value merge in REST/ALB vs raw string in V2) and headers (multi-value merge vs comma-split). Request and response assembly group different field sets, giving three-plus purposes with two-plus different decisions.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt names the four clump types and the three-by-three flavor scope. The solver inspects each EventToRequest/GetProxyResponse to find the named construction/query/header helpers across 6 core files — several steps along a local call chain, classifiable without combining other components. No cross-component data flow; adapters are explicitly out of scope.

repair_coordination.evidence: A shared stage-data abstraction (e.g., one RequestAssemblyInput struct or shared helper spanning the 3 flavors) requires all 3 flavors' callers and helpers to adopt the same shape. If only one flavor changes, the stage is not 'expressed once' and the consolidation is inconsistent. Multiple locations must preserve the shared abstraction rule.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform struct extraction cleanly covers only the 3 identical-signature assembleCoreRequest locations (about 25% of the ~12 clump occurrences). The response clump needs a different struct; query and header clumps have V2 variants needing their own field sets, so a single uniform rule cannot cover them.

behavioral_risk.evidence: A wrong abstraction that drops or miswires rawMethod/rawPath — used only in assembleCoreRequest's error-path fmt.Printf log — compiles and passes ordinary calls, but produces wrong log output only when http.NewRequest fails, a special state not covered by equality assertions. Score-4 conditions (a second hidden path with test evidence) are not established.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
